comments.body:
Here is a somewhat cleaned up HLO module that also reproduces the error

```
HloModule elmwise

ENTRY main {
  param_0 = bf16[1,2,3072] parameter(0)
  param_1 = f32[1,2,4096] parameter(1) 
  param_2 = f32[2,4096] parameter(2)
  param_3 = bf16[2,4096,3072] parameter(3)
  convert.1 = f32[2,4096,3072] convert(param_3)
  broadcast.1 = f32[2,4096,3072] broadcast(param_2), dimensions={0,1}
  subtract.1 = f32[2,4096,3072] subtract(convert.1, broadcast.1)
  bitcast.1 = f32[2,4096] bitcast(param_1)
  broadcast.2 = f32[2,4096,3072] broadcast(bitcast.1), dimensions={0,1}
  multiply.1 = f32[2,4096,3072] multiply(subtract.1, broadcast.2)
  convert.2 = bf16[2,4096,3072] convert(multiply.1)
  bitcast.2 = bf16[2,3072] bitcast(param_0)
  broadcast.3 = bf16[2,4096,3072] broadcast(bitcast.2), dimensions={0,2}
  multiply.2 = bf16[2,4096,3072] multiply(convert.2, broadcast.3)
  ROOT add.2 = bf16[2,4096,3072] add(multiply.2, param_3)
}
```

@sergachev just told me that bitcasts are not supposed to be present in unoptimized HLO? If so, we should detect that in the HLO verifier and error with that, instead of the layout error we get later. Or we can fix the layout propagation. Opinions welcome.

Bitcasts only have a meaning after layouts are assigned. Therefore they should indeed not be present in unoptimized HLO. But it is possible to replace them while keeping the semantics the same. We have logic that can decompose a bitcast into transpose - reshape - transpose

https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/0f4399bb12952e7112e29d8740685cc13a1e7bf5/xla/shape_util.h#L884

(the transposes on either side can be the identity in some cases).
When doing that replacement, layout propagation should work just fine.

Hi @dimvar,

Closing the issue because we believe the question has been answered, Please feel free to reopen the issue if you still have a concern. Thanks!
